Occurrences.Kwic: 僧擬議，師連打喝出，僧便走。師喚僧來，僧回身，師云：「更要一頓麼？」問：「世尊不說說，迦葉不聞聞。」師遂喝云：「你是一箇無狀賊漢。」僧無語，師打出。僧舉：「太陽明安問僧：『何處來？』僧云：『洪山來。』明云：『先師在麼？』僧云：『在。』明云：『在即不無，請渠出來，我要相見。』僧云：『聻？』明云：『此猶是侍者。』僧無對。山翁和尚代云：『明朝更獻楚王看。』」師云：「道則忒煞道，只得八成。」僧云：「和尚又作麼生？」師云：「不可降尊就卑。」僧禮拜，師大笑云：「又是侍者去也。」僧求開示，師云：「我不如你。」僧云：「和尚知即得。」師云：「擔枷過狀。」便打。師問僧：「倩女離魂，那個是真底？」僧云：「亂走作麼？」師云：「你為什麼蹋破草鞋？」僧擬議，師喝出。師問僧：「來此作什麼？」僧云：「親覲和尚。」師云：「一場敗闕。」僧云：「和尚莫錯舉。」師云：「蝦蟆窟裏活計。」僧禮拜，師云：「莫是舊時會過的麼？」僧云：「沒有。」師云：「沒有便罷。」僧拜已，侍立，師云：「作麼？作麼？」僧云：「求開示。」師云：「龍蛇混雜，凡聖交參。」僧無語，師云：「參。」僧問：「獨居空山，忽若鬼怪精魅一齊圍繞時如何？」師云：「善哉！善哉！」僧云：「意旨如何？」師云：「青黃赤白黑。」僧相訪，問：「如何是和尚家風？」師云：「家裏精窮，客來便打。」云：「請和尚打看。

Senses.Explanation: Qiannu’s soul leaves her body is the compact name of a public case centered on the question “which one is real?” Wuzu Fayan asks the foundational question. An unnamed monk puts it to Baishan Dekai, and Yunwai Xingze asks it of another monk. A lamp biography reports Fojian Huiqin repeatedly raising the case until an obstruction opened. The entry records the case formula and its use without choosing one “real” Qiannu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 徹曰：『山僧麤識好惡。』天童覺禪師曰：『若有問長蘆，便和聲打。為甚如此？我從來不識好惡。』」師曰：「芭蕉雖識好惡，大似醉後添杯，要活者僧不得。天童不識好惡，是則驅耕奪食，雖活者僧，未免傷鋒犯手。若有問新豐，但向道：『利劍不斬死漢。』若是箇衲僧，管取別有生涯。」師曰：「雖然，不免打破蔡州。」頻吉祥禪師語錄卷第十三終頻吉祥禪師語錄卷第十四嗣法門人德然等編頌古一頌古釋迦牟尼世尊初降生時，一手指天，一手指地，周行七步，目顧四方曰：「天上天下，唯我獨尊。」

Occurrences.Kwic: 尺竿頭如何進步。泉云。更進一步。僧復問瓦官。官云。百尺竿頭用進作什麼。僧不肯。官便打。師云。大眾。古人機變出在一時。其間別有商量。亦未言著。且如雪竇。今日再入靈隱。也似百尺竿頭。依南泉之言。得進一步。喜與大眾相見。則十方世界一時周匝。便下座。師到越州承天寺。眾請陞座。僧問。學人不問西來意。藏身北斗意如何。師云。拈頭作尾漢。進云。請師答話。師云。西天令嚴。問有問有答賓主歷然。無問無答時如何。師云。古路草漫漫。進云。若不上來。焉知與麼。師云利劍不斬死漢。師乃云。作者相見。一拶一捺。撩起便行。若佇思停機。卒摸𢱢不著。若言問在答處答在問宗。箇箇依草附木。問不在答處答不在問宗。罕見頂上有眼。諸人還薦得也無。薦得薦不得。並是新雪竇之過。且莫鈍致承天和尚。越州檀越備茶筵。請師陞座。僧問。檀越殷勤伸三請。乞師方便指迷津。師云。不許夜行投明須到。進云。非但學人。四眾有賴。師云。百千年後問如何是祖師西來意。師云。迢迢十萬餘。僧禮拜。師云。拄杖不在。師乃云。諸檀信。山僧暫以經過。邂逅相遇。何沐特隆異待

Senses.Explanation: A sharp sword does not cut a dead man: the saying closes an encounter by judging that further cutting cannot enliven the respondent. Pinjixiang Zhixiang and Yuanjie Jingying use the saying to close exchanges by contrasting a sharp sword with a man already dead. Xuedou Chongxian and Chushi Fanqi likewise turn the sword-and-dead-man image into a verdict on the respondent rather than advice about weapons.

Senses.Explanation: Throughout heaven and earth names the whole world-span; in Chan records it is repeatedly loaded by the Buddha-birth declaration and then reused as an answer, a question, and a scope claim. Zhaozhou Congshen answers a question about not picking and choosing with 'throughout heaven and earth, I alone am honored.' In Changqing Da'an's record, a monk quotes the same line and asks who its 'I' is. Dahui Zonggao speaks of a person whom nothing throughout heaven and earth can manage, while Yuanwu Keqin and Hongzhi Zhengjue use the phrase for unrestricted whole-world scope. Those uses keep the bare headword broader than the birth formula alone.

Senses.Explanation: "In heaven the moon is full; among people the moon is half full" places two moon appearances in one saying. Senses.Explanation: The stars facing north and waters flowing east form a fixed image of common orientation toward one center. Mian Jie uses the pair in a Thousand-Autumn imperial address; other hall addresses speak it directly, while two monks offer it in exchanges and receive replies from Yangshan and Baichi. Both clauses express convergence: celestial bodies incline north and terrestrial waters run east. Their reuse in formal addresses makes that shared orientation the Chan use.

Entries.SourceTerm: 天上無彌勒，地下無彌勒

Senses.PreferredTarget: No Maitreya in heaven, no Maitreya on earth
AlternateTargets: Maitreya is neither above in heaven nor below on earth
Senses.Note: A lecturer says Maitreya is in heaven and has not yet descended. Nanquan replies with this paired denial. Sanyi reopens the name question, Yongji directly reverses both clauses, Liangting brings in the Dongshan-Yunju sequel, Huizhou raises a fist against the expected answer, Tiebi extends the pair into a new verse, and Juelang tests how the old pair unsettles a present hearer. The exact inherited pair is Nanquan's; the five later masters supply different current responses.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 見歇祖。八字打開，別施手眼；衣被萬物，乳育群英，使箇箇遮天蓋地去。還會麼？夜排月戶清光遠，山拭秋稜秀色多。立僧上堂。乃喝曰：「看！沉毛江上波湧，鐵船忽爾浮來；沒底藍裏風動，玉花驀地笑開。瞿曇漏失消息，達磨脫落皮鞋。是誰於此扶豎佛祖綱宗，表正人天眼目；振大機而展大用，擢群秀而拔群才？神珠影吞海嶽，寶劍飛拂塵埃；不勞敲骨出髓，自能地轉天迴。且道今日皋亭立僧底節文在甚麼處？欲親拶入遮那藏，好見文殊腦後腮。」結制上堂：十字街頭結制，唯有石橛子自敢承當；急水灘上白椎，秪許竹篙兒全機活脫。杖人恁麼舉，忽有箇出來捲卻席子，也好與三十棒。且道是賞伊罰伊？簡點得出，黃頭碧眼剜肉成瘡；簡點不出，白牯黧奴開眼作夢。秪如今日與眾造箇款端又作麼生？巨靈抬手無多子，擘破華山千萬重。青原專使送衲衣至上堂：曹溪得髓，超超豎拂；青原廬米，吹毛凜凜全提。震旦師承各稟，誰破天荒？敲唱同時，獨標宗眼在。昔行倒竿之令方，今逗微笑之機，怪習氣以舞琴聲，奇金襴而佇雞足。秪如天上無彌勒，地下無彌勒，直得雲巖禪床震動、洞山遍體汗流時又作麼生？閒拈拄杖風前立，看鶴飛鳴上九皋。壽昌南嶽兩專使至上堂：先聖曰：「寄諸空言，不如行諸實事。」與其舉古，何似驗今？秪如壽昌兩長老之交代，亦可法也。還知竺菴成公之行履麼？獨龍擺尾風雷迅；雙鳳啣珠氣象新。扶起祖竿，不恃成功汗馬；呼來弟喏，能催躍浪神鱗。到處好山春色秀，隨方相見倍相親；橫拈鈯斧歸衡嶽，誰識石頭滑殺人？如此已是一擲骰子滿盤紅，何待遙觀添喝彩？況此原是渠之出身處也。須有俊快衲僧，竿木隨身者去探他一噓兩噓。或如豹披霧而毛文；象聞雷而牙燦，不使古祖宗，猷益遠大乎？雖然，更須知光雪存公之出處。石耳凌空，鏟佛殿前之夙草；鼓峰放箭，騎聖僧上之危肩。此子天然踏翻釣艇，直得通身頑爛，於濃滴滴處遍著艾焦，始悟天界杖下骨疼，掘起向大好山、無縫影裏叫屈，撞著同門冤對特地鈍置，恨更難消，飛符皋鶴亭前，惹杖人一笑。且道笑箇甚麼？疾風知勁卉，傲雪見新條。汪本和比部施材倡造大殿請上堂。拈拄杖曰：「向上不傳，腳底踏通諸聖路；獨尊在我，杖頭點發大千機。所以從門入者不是家珍，直須向自己胸中迸出，始能遮天蓋地，到此也須知者箇消息始得。碧眼胡留嵩山半片影石，震旦敷五葉之花；陳亞仙創曹溪一座祖庭，萬世傳二株之命。以故青

Entries.SourceTerm: 天上無雙月，人間只一僧

Senses.PreferredTarget: There is no second moon in the sky, and only one monk among people.
AlternateTargets: Heaven has no twin moon; among people there is but one monk.
SearchAliases: No second moon only one monk
One moon in heaven one monk on earth
Senses.Note: Qianyan uses the single moon and single monk in a verse on Zhaozhou. In Tiantong's record an unnamed monk offers the pair as praise, which Tiantong rejects as staining him. In Jiqi's hall another monk points to the crowd and asks how there can be so many if only one monk is meant; Jiqi refuses a ready explanation. A third unnamed monk says it to Shending, who warns against calling a bell a jar. The paired image is stable, but its use is challenged in each conversation.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 天上無雙月，人間只一僧

Senses.Explanation: One moon in the sky is paired with the claim that only one monk stands among people. Qianyan voices it in a verse on Zhaozhou; an unnamed monk tries to praise Tiantong with it and is turned back. Separate unnamed monks raise it to Jiqi and Shending; their answers test the phrase rather than accepting it as praise.

Senses.Explanation: Peace throughout the realm is the ordinary condition of a peaceful country and people. Yulin Tongxiu pairs it with the people's welfare, Miyun Yuanwu with their secure livelihoods, and Juelang Daosheng with an imperial blessing. Yunmen Wenyan names it as the result he would seek by striking the newborn Buddha; Zhongfeng Mingben and Tianyin Yuanxiu later raise and appraise that line. Yangzhuo Zhengming also lists a peaceful realm as a practical reason not to remain in solitary retreat.

Senses.Note: Feiyin offers the full pair as his own answer when asked what the ancestors transmit. Yichu answers a request for teaching at an opening hall, Xiangya uses it for a completed hermitage, and Tianshu sets it into a New Year verse. The public shorter clause speaks of peace under heaven; the second clause extends that peace to the daily life of the people.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 便是愁米。正愁悶間，忽有個人來報道：『莫愁悶，且從容，草玄閣上子雲公，數日已前曾有約，今朝一定到山中。齋也有，嚫也有，每人一個大饅首。』不特山僧生歡喜，彌勒如來開笑口，肚皮喫得飽膨脝，面對南山看北斗。」復舉：「歸宗禪師因僧問：『如何是佛？』宗云：『即汝便是。』僧云：『如何保任？』宗云：『一翳在眼，空花亂墜。』」師云：「歸宗恁麼荅話，也是就釘打鐵。這僧雖解承當，爭奈腳底未穩。山僧則不然，若有問：『如何是佛？』向他道：『拄杖子。』『如何保任？』」良久，云：「扶過斷橋水，伴歸明月村。」下座。小參小參早參。師云：「今朝冬至一陽生，石筍抽條賀太平，惟有山僧拄杖子，不屬陰陽不變更。」遂拈起拄杖，云：「為甚昨日拄杖子走出山門外，四大部洲遶一匝方回？莫道四大部洲遶一匝，饒他遶遍無邊剎土，總離我這裏不得。」卓拄杖，下座。早參。師云：「山僧今早拈香禮佛、祝聖拜年已畢，金山塔為筆、楊子江為墨、太虛為紙，大書四句偈。且道：那四句偈？歲朝把筆，百事大吉，天下太平，萬民樂業。」早參。師云：「諸方過冬鬧浩浩，鶴林過冬靜悄悄，池邊鴨子凍匾嘴，斗裏蝦兒都不跳。跳一跳，三十棒，要不要？何故聻？勤底卻被懶底笑。今朝節屆書雲灰飛葭管。還有不屬陰陽消長者麼？出來道道。」時有僧作禮，云：「請和尚證明。」師云：「證明個甚麼？」僧擬議，師便打，乃云：「山僧若也道出，極是現成、極是巧妙。且道：是那一句？」驀拈拄杖，指云：「濂溪祠向米家墳，摩笄山對張王廟。」中秋，早參。師云：「大眾！昨夜可曾看見月華麼？」以兩手作圓月樣，云：「始初這樣大。」以兩手又放開些，云：「漸漸這樣大。」乃大拓開兩手，旋風繞云：「後來這樣大、這樣大，無邊無際，普天匝地，明察秋毫，不容擬議。咦！可惜好個境界，那時諸人總在睡夢中，影也不知。」呵呵大笑，歸方丈。早參。師云：「昨日舊歲，今朝新年，祝延皇帝聖壽萬年，普天之下慶賀豐年。若老、若少，身添一年；若僧、若俗，大家拜年。且道：拜年相見一句作麼生？春風滿面人情喜，必定今年勝去年。」晚參。師云：「禪須參個實頭禪，不在腳尖語句邊，若是有人親撞著，馬師碑在寺門前。還有撞著者麼？若撞著，自應頭破腦裂，血流滿地；若道撞不著，終日出出入入，為甚當面蹉過？」晚參。「山僧嘗見人說醫星落在鎮江，所以名醫甚多，四方來就醫

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi. Baichi Xingyuan owns the retained deployment, naming the corps' dusk-eight-hundred and dawn-three-thousand drubbing as its daily fare.

Senses.Explanation: A collective address that sweeps every elder master of the age into one body. Yunmen Wenyan dares the whole corps, after the twelvefold teaching, to bring him a needle-tip of the way, Chijue Daochong counts them into the single-file succession from Bodhidharma onward, Dahui Zonggao finds that when the tree falls and the vine dries even they have nowhere to breathe, Tanfang Shouzhong ranks the three sets of buddhas, patriarchs, and every elder master below the one standing there, and Baichi Xingyuan has them drubbing eight hundred at dusk and three thousand at dawn as their daily fare. Linji Yixuan says his eye cleared only after meeting a great teacher, so that he could tell the corps' crooked from straight, Muchen Daomin grants that even the buddhas, patriarchs, and every elder master cannot leap past the place, Yinyuan Longqi has them splashing sky and earth while the shrimp still cannot leave the ladle, Yuejiang Zhengyin calls them all fortune-tellers, and Ying'an Tanhua hangs the buddhas' mouths on the wall and asks what the corps eats with.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Seek a healer throughout the world, then cauterize the pig's left shoulder
SearchAliases: seek a healer throughout the world, then cauterize the pig's left shoulder
Senses.Note: Dushun's verse says that a cow eats grain in one place and a horse's belly swells elsewhere; its final pair sends everyone looking for a doctor, only to cauterize a pig's left shoulder. Jinian attaches deliberately unhelpful annotations. Qianyan says verbal explanations miss Dushun, while Wuqu answers in verse. Baichi asks how it fits Huayan, Sanshan offers a different remedy, and Xuzhou joins it to Fu Dashi's paradoxical bridge verse. The displaced cure tests the impulse to settle the verse by ordinary cause and effect.

Senses.Explanation: A fixed oneness formula, heaven and earth of one root, inherited from the treatise writer and spent by the turn. Dahui Zonggao grounds the deathless uncoming mind in it, so that every thing arriving on the mind empties at once, Wansong Xingxiu reads Xuedou's verse of it beside the old master's dream-like peony and ranks the two against the moon dropped in the empty pool, Chushi Fanqi opens the summer's release with it, filling valley and pit, out-measuring a space that still has a name and outshining a sun that still casts light, and Tianyin Yuanxiu retells the official's quoting of the line and answers it in his own turn with one lift of the whisk, everything gathered there. Poshan Haiming reads the unhurried seasons through it, one mind for sage and commoner and one way for past and present, Miyun Yuanwu checks the autumn proverb against it and finds that whoever screens the saying can meet the one root of heaven and earth without trouble, Yinyuan Longqi traces the birthday star of staff-holder, household, beasts, and grasses to one resting place and names it, and Yulin Tongxiu writes it at the head of the life-saving verse, that the original face has no this and no other, so sparing lives is sparing one's own stock.

Senses.Explanation: Heaven and earth share one root; the myriad things form one body. The inherited unity claim tests direct seeing beyond separate objects. Selected current source uses: Buhui Fatong in J32nB276, Poshan Haiming in J26nB177, Feiyin Tongrong in J26nB178, Miyun Yuanwu in J10nA158, Tianyin Yuanxiu in J25nB171, Jieweizhou Xingzhou in J28nB205. The complete wording is the entry unit. One body does not erase distinctions among beings or acts.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Heaven and earth are empty even of Qin's sun and moon; mountains and rivers show no Han ruler or ministers.

Senses.Note: Qin and Han supply poetic imperial markers, not an astronomical statement or encounter date. The closing use tests remaining reactive attachment rather than approving every outward claim to freedom.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是奪人不奪境？曰：家裏已無回日信，路邊空有望鄉牌。云：如何是奪境不奪人？曰：滄海盡教枯到底，青山直得碾為塵。云：如何是人境兩俱奪？曰：天地尚空秦日月，山河不見漢君臣。云：如何是人境俱不奪？曰：鶯囀千林華滿地，客游三月草侵天。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X79/X79n1559.xml). Jiatai Universal Lamp Record. A monk asks Jinshan Tanying about the four alternatives of removing the person while leaving the environment, removing the environment while leaving the person, removing both, and removing neither. Jinshan first answers with a household lacking return news and a distant road's homesickness marker; then he has the sea dried out and green mountains crushed to dust. Asked about removing both person and environment, he gives the Qin-and-Han pair. Asked about removing neither, he answers with birds singing through a thousand woods, flowers covering the ground and a traveler's springtime grass reaching the sky. The headword occupies one specific place in this sequence: its absent imperial lights, ruler and ministers answer the double removal. These are poetic contrasts, not a claim that actual celestial bodies disappeared after a dynasty ended.

Occurrences.Kwic: 二乘見解，猶如困魚止瀝、病鳥栖蘆。舉步出門，便有兩條岐路：不憎凡，便愛聖；不厭生死，便趣涅槃；不樂天堂，便惡地獄。此輩人雖入聖流，依然凡夫境界，若能揩磨執著心病，自然生死籠罩佗不得，於生死中著著自有出身之分。凡無一物不從清淨智中顯發殊勝玅力，至於經行、坐臥、俯仰、折旋，無一處而非佛事、無一則而非莊嚴。所以，南泉老人道：『王老師自小養一頭水牯牛，擬向谿東牧，不免犯佗國王水艸；擬向谿西牧，不免犯佗國王水艸。不如隨分納些些，總不見得。』於此會去，荒田不揀，用得親切，進則逢緣作主，任意而行；退則透出法身，片雲不挂。燦燦一天，歷歷未動，不彰而彰、不現而現，曰賢、曰聖，平等一如，是寒、是暑，隨佗遷變，去住自由，如鳥無異，更有甚麼管帶？更有甚麼根塵？雖然如是，內有箇漢忿性出來，收了止靜牌，推出大眾去，掉臂而行，更不如何若何。我說是人，未曾悟在。莫是山僧屈人麼？」良久，云：「天地尚空秦日月，山河不見漢君臣。」喝一喝，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB343.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyin of Shengjue Monastery, Guangfu Mountain. Miyin Zhenchuan criticizes practitioners who merely choose holy over ordinary, release over birth and death, or heaven over hell. Citing Nanquan's difficulty pasturing his water buffalo without trespassing, he describes intimate handling that can advance freely or withdraw beyond the truth body, moving with cold and heat without attachment. Yet suppose someone inside becomes angry, takes away the silence signal, pushes the assembly out and strides away without further discussion: Miyin says that person has not awakened. Is he wronging the person? After a pause he gives the Qin-and-Han pair, shouts and descends. The couplet closes an address that tests apparent freedom against remaining reactive attachment. The record does not explain the image as a license for the angry departure or identify a newly approved person behind that performance.

Senses.Explanation: The heaven-and-earth-apart of the Chan records: the greatest gap, set between the sizing mind and seeing-nature, between letters and the living address, between the snow-cry and the insect in the wood, and between two householders' verses. Huangbo Xiyun warns the student who has built a right-and-wrong mind and a defiled-and-pure mind, learned one knowing and one understanding, and walks the whole world sizing people — who has the eye, who is strong, who weak — that measured so, it is heaven and earth apart, so what more is there to say of seeing-nature, Linji Yixuan prices the letter-seekers: aiming only at the buddha-way inside words, they guess it by opinion — poles apart; way-folk, the mountain monk speaks a teaching — what teaching? the mind-ground teaching, entering the holy and the common, the pure and the defiled, the true and the conventional, yet it is none of your holy-common-true-conventional, Ying'an Tanhua raises Zhaozhou's snow-cry — Save me! Save me! — and the monk who lay down beside him while Zhaozhou rose and left, grading that monk like the insect boring wood that by accident writes a character: to see Zhaozhou, heaven and earth apart — and the blind crowd that cries Bao'en backs the strong and not the weak does not know the king's treasury holds no such knife, and Jianfu Chenggu rules that even seeing rightly and exactly serves on the layman's ground, but on the patched-robe's ground it is heaven and earth apart — so, assembly, what is the patched-robe's ground-matter? Say it and see. Yanxi Guangwen at the solstice: the elders said it so, Wanshou raises it so — only you must not take it so; to take it so is heaven and earth apart, Huanyou Zhengchuan sets the two lay verses against each other — Layman Pang's daily affair of no-other and self-harmony, hauling water and carrying firewood, measured against the elder Fu's nightly sleeping arm-in-arm with the buddha: heaven and earth apart, not matching one householder — then asks his all-householder audience what their daily affair is, Yuan'an Liao rules that such matching is exactly the man-burying pit — under Shending, heaven and earth apart: does one not see it said, the way-man walks where fire melts ice, the arrow once off the string has no returning force, and Yikui Yuankui at the donor feast — of all offerings the teaching-offering is greatest, the patron's gold already in your bowls and bellies — sets the patched-robe's ground poles apart: is it the thus-come's Chan, the founder's intent, Deshan's staff, Linji's shout? Happily, no connection at all.

Senses.Explanation: Heaven and earth hang apart. Chushi Fanqi doubles the saying in one breath — with a hair's difference heaven and earth hang apart, and without a hair's difference heaven and earth still hang apart — then adds that even understanding it is only poking one's head out of a toad's den; Liangting Jingting sets it against the moment of the unthinkable, where one phrase-topic covers all coming deceit; Tianru Weize reads it at the fault-line of one buddha-nature and one wondrous function, where defiled habit alone splits them; and Linji Yixuan, in the sermon Dahui's anthology keeps, brands seeking the meaning through words and letters as far from the dharma as heaven from earth. Gaofeng Yuanmiao grants Yunmen and Yuanwu the crown-eye yet rules their wellsprings worlds apart, Hanyue Fazang says the affair from above is not gotten from another and that cutting off the left arm itself leaves heaven and earth hanging apart, Konggu Daocheng answers a monk's flourished sleeve with the bare doubled saying, Gulin Qingmao answers an inaugural exchange with it in four graphs, Zhongfeng Mingben stamps it into his verse — a hair astray, heaven and earth apart — and mocks glossators who squat in clarity, and Jizong Che rules of two departed worthies that to call them the same leaves heaven and earth hanging apart while to call them different loses the question of coming and going.

Senses.Explanation: The two destinations: heaven and hell as one pair — what masters dissolve, walk through unmoved, or hand back as a question. Caoshan Benji, after raising Nanquan's line that even ten-tenths still falls one thread short, tells the trainee that at this point one must be clear and free: heaven or hell, hungry ghost or beast, in every place unmoved — the same old person, only not walking the old road, and the moment there is fondness, entanglement returns; the treatise voice of Bodhidharma rules that with one thought rising there are the two deeds and the pair is there, with no thought rising neither deeds nor pair remain — in the ordinary it is there, in the sage it is not; Xitang Zhizang, whose case Dahui Zonggao retells, answers the laughing layman that there-is holds for the man with a wife and children and greed like the sea, while the master without a wife may rightly say there-is-not — look how the old ones came out; Zhenjing Kewen, asked about the realm-field by the Garland lecturer, lifts his staff: not the realm-field but the shining, vast, quiet core of every one of them — this shore and other shores, heaven and hell, the six common and four sage orders, feeling and unfeeling, all one, unbroken, unmixed, like the emperor-net's pearls. Miyun Yuanwu, asked by a layman who cannot match the master's ease — what then of heaven and hell? — turns it back: what do you even call the pair? have you ever been there?; Tianran Hanshi warns his trainees off the ready-made line that heaven and hell are an old monk's everyday tea and rice — say it if you like, but when the breath fails it will still come down to whether your awakening holds; Qianyan Yuanzhang tells the assembly that while the wild mind is unresting even heaven does not please and becoming a buddha is an empty shell, but once it rests, not even buddha needs doing — so why still speak of heaven and hell; Wuming Huijing names this one that gives birth to sky and earth, to buddhas and immortals, to men and women, to sages and worthies, to heaven and hell, to hungry ghosts and beasts — and beyond all that, gives birth to the unborn.

Senses.Explanation: A heavenly woman is a female celestial figure; this entry's selected cases center on the woman who encounters Shariputra in the Vimalakirti record. Chan masters raise her transformation of Shariputra, question her sex, and separately recall her scattering flowers as inherited case material. Outside those cases, the word remains an ordinary reference to a celestial woman.

Senses.Note: Yunmen’s old answer evokes a cold short day and one bowl shared by two. Wuming Huixing cites the line but offers a competing, more ample answer. Po’an Zuxian makes it his own answer to a monk who presses him to speak. Chushi Fanqi uses it to answer how one comes home, while Yu’an Zhiji uses it in a direct exchange about practice. The bowl is a concrete response, not a general rule about poverty.

Senses.Explanation: “The day is cold and short; two people share one bowl” answers high questions with an immediate winter meal. Wuming explicitly quotes Yunmen and challenges his austerity; Po’an uses the old wording as a direct answer in a new exchange. Chushi gives it as the phrase for getting home, and Yu’an offers it amid a challenge about his condition.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB362.xml). In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guantaoqi, Guantao first criticizes attachment to opposed views and asks what force a lion uses in taking either an elephant or a rabbit. In a later hall address he contrasts the noise of many people with one person speaking plainly, mentions household implements, and rejects classifications as with or without leakage, or as large or small, when seeing remains partial. Then he asks the assembly, 'A cold day is short; two people share one bowl: what aspect does this illuminate?' He immediately warns that grasping it without measure leads down a wrong road. The winter-meal line is Guantao's present challenge, not an answer he supplies; the source warns against fixing its sense too quickly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin, Feiyin gives a paired hall formulation: 'Striking left and right: a cold day is short, two people share one bowl; calling ahead and answering behind: wind blows and sun bakes an old broken earthen bowl.' He then says that if the assembly understands these two expressions, a nun is still a woman; otherwise an old monk must preach, and he follows with another pointed image. The meal line is one half of Feiyin's present verbal pairing, not a quotation credited to the monk in the preceding separate exchange. Its paired blows, calls, and replies matter more locally than a claim about a particular historical meal.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian’an Sheng, a monk asks whether offerings formerly brought by heavenly beings and a lay patron's present meal are the same or different. Tian'an answers with the cold short day and two people sharing one bowl. The monk tests that answer by asking how anyone could eat a meal of iron nails and a soup of wooden slats; Tian'an says the monk cannot swallow it. When the monk offers another flourish about a golden rooster and a grain of millet, Tian'an asks where he learned that. The shared bowl answers the same-or-different question through a concrete meal image, and the next turns test whether the monk can actually handle that answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe’an Fan, the line describes the temple's actual winter provision as Zhe'an speaks to his community. He names coarse rice from the mountain fields, plain wild greens, and the cold short days on which two people share a bowl, saying this happens daily without a shortage. He says the long-assembled monks have shared sweetness and hardship, and that he knows them; he trusts they will not blame him and can rest at ease. Here the meal image is anchored in material communal life before he turns to life's passing and closes with a shout. Treating it only as a free-floating metaphor would erase that setting.

Senses.Explanation:
'The day is cold and short; two people share one bowl' joins cold short days and a shared meal. Its five witnesses use the same words in different turns.

In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guantaoqi, Guantao first criticizes attachment to opposed views and asks what force a lion uses in taking either an elephant or a rabbit. In a later hall address he contrasts the noise of many people with one person speaking plainly, mentions household implements, and rejects classifications as with or without leakage, or as large or small, when seeing remains partial. Then he asks the assembly, 'A cold day is short; two people share one bowl: what aspect does this illuminate?' He immediately warns that grasping it without measure leads down a wrong road. The winter-meal line is Guantao's present challenge, not an answer he supplies; the source warns against fixing its sense too quickly.

In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin, Feiyin gives a paired hall formulation: 'Striking left and right: a cold day is short, two people share one bowl; calling ahead and answering behind: wind blows and sun bakes an old broken earthen bowl.' He then says that if the assembly understands these two expressions, a nun is still a woman; otherwise an old monk must preach, and he follows with another pointed image. The meal line is one half of Feiyin's present verbal pairing, not a quotation credited to the monk in the preceding separate exchange. Its paired blows, calls, and replies matter more locally than a claim about a particular historical meal.

In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian’an Sheng, a monk asks whether offerings formerly brought by heavenly beings and a lay patron's present meal are the same or different. Tian'an answers with the cold short day and two people sharing one bowl. The monk tests that answer by asking how anyone could eat a meal of iron nails and a soup of wooden slats; Tian'an says the monk cannot swallow it. When the monk offers another flourish about a golden rooster and a grain of millet, Tian'an asks where he learned that. The shared bowl answers the same-or-different question through a concrete meal image, and the next turns test whether the monk can actually handle that answer.

In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe’an Fan, the line describes the temple's actual winter provision as Zhe'an speaks to his community. He names coarse rice from the mountain fields, plain wild greens, and the cold short days on which two people share a bowl, saying this happens daily without a shortage. He says the long-assembled monks have shared sweetness and hardship, and that he knows them; he trusts they will not blame him and can rest at ease. Here the meal image is anchored in material communal life before he turns to life's passing and closes with a shout. Treating it only as a free-floating metaphor would erase that setting.

Senses.Explanation: The heaven-clear-earth-still couplet of the Chan records: the old book's oneness borrowed and broken open — the sovereign's one stilling the realm, and the patch-robe monk's one: seedlings cut at the ground, eyes level and nose straight, the almsbowl's mouth to the sky. Baiyun Shouduan hangs the new hall tablet and the monk rides the couplet in: heaven, gaining the one, becomes clear; earth, gaining the one, becomes still; the sovereign, gaining the one, governs the realm — what is the patch-robe monk's one fit for? Seedlings cut off at the ground. Then — so it is huddling to the fire in cold, eating when hungry? A hundred and eight thousand. Yes? — The assembly sees you. The monk bows, Yuelin Shiguan opens the year: heaven by the one clear, earth by the one still, the sovereign's one governing the realm — and the patch-robe monk's one? Eyes level, nose straight. Imperial grace and the buddhas' grace, repaid in one stroke, Qianyan Yuanzhang raises the elder's turn: Yangqi asked it of old — what is the patch-robe monk's one fit for? — waited, then: the almsbowl's mouth turned up to the sky. And his own grade: big Yangqi or little Yangqi, the well-worn words stick; so what is the patch-robe monk's one? — one crack of the staff, one shout, down from the seat. Sanyi Mingyu works the couplet with his whisk: lift it out from right here — raise the one, do not raise the two: heaven by the one clear, earth by the one still, the lords' one and the realm at peace. The whisk rises: it draws out the Recumbing Dragon's Liangfu chant. Cracks: listen, Xiangya Xingting opens the new year on his staff: heaven by the one clear, earth by the one still — the first day founding the year, the ten thousand things made new; village songs and shrine dances, the way's-law plain — the unbusied patch-robe monk wishes the realm its long peace. One crack of the staff, down from the seat, and Banshui Fayuan takes the memorial seat for Lord Luo: heaven by the one clear, earth by the one still — only the Three-Peak has nothing to gain, taking up the staff outright to offer the passage-over. Assembly, do you see? Three cracks of the staff: the six roots just stirring — clouded over; one thought unborn — the whole body present.

SearchAliases: heaven gains it and becomes clear; earth gains it and becomes settled
Senses.Note: The line says heaven is clear and earth is settled through what each “gets.” In these sermons the unnamed “it” remains open to a question rather than becoming an object. Sanyi turns from the seasons toward his assembly, Huiyue punctuates a New Year’s talk with a staff sign, Daxiao extends the list to rulers and monks, and Biemu brings it into a funeral address before striking the table.

Senses.Explanation: The old heaven-and-earth parallel becomes a way to ask what each speaker means by “it.” Sanyi speaks the pair while pressing his listeners beyond seasonal order. Huiyue draws a sign with his staff and makes the pair answer a New Year’s hall talk. Daxiao adds kings, officials, and monks to the sequence. Biemu extends it through family relations to a woman being mourned and then gives a concrete table strike.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1996.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue. Xuedou Chongxian's own collected verse contains a headed poem called 'Five Elders' Lion.' Its opening pictures a force crouching on earth and coiling into the sky without resting, then asks why its claws and fangs need compete with the passing crowd. The closing pair says that heaven placed it above a thousand peaks and that it stands out even without clouds lifting it. The title and image present the peak as a lion and emphasize its imposing height. The pair asserts an elevation that does not depend on the cloud's support, rather than reporting a creature physically lifted by clouds. The poem is directly preserved in Xuedou's collected verses, rather than known only through later accounts. A later historical account explicitly attributes the related Lion Peak poem to Xuedou, though its opening couplet has different wording. The complete headword pair is stable apart from the attested two spellings of peak.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB395.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qizhencheng of Neihuguo Monastery, Jingnan. When patrons give robes at Qizhen Cheng's hall address, he first offers a verse questioning how an ascetic comes by gold brocade and invoking Tiger Stream's immeasurable appearance for everyone to see. He lifts the robe, calls the assembly to look carefully, puts it on and takes his seat. He says that a lion's den contains only lions and a sandalwood grove only sandalwood, adding that a great person has great vision and great wisdom has great activity. He then introduces an older four-line lion poem with an unnamed quotation formula, including the exact heaven-and-cloud pair, and descends from the seat. The local quoted verse voice is unnamed; Qizhen is the present quoter using its elevated lion image in the robe-gift setting. A parallel is directly preserved among Xuedou's poems, but Qizhen does not name that author here. His gesture and comparisons direct the assembly toward the capacity of the person rather than simply the robe's appearance. The source does not establish a literal transformation into a lion or give the robe an independently magical power. This performed application is distinct from the original landscape poem; historical and anthology copies of that poem add no further current family.

Senses.Explanation: Heaven placed it above a thousand peaks; even without clouds to lift it, it stands out. Xuedou Chongxian's own collected verse contains a headed poem called 'Five Elders' Lion.' Its opening pictures a force crouching on earth and coiling into the sky without resting, then asks why its claws and fangs need compete with the passing crowd. The closing pair says that heaven placed it above a thousand peaks and that it stands out even without clouds lifting it. The title and image present the peak as a lion and emphasize its imposing height. The pair asserts an elevation that does not depend on the cloud's support, rather than reporting a creature physically lifted by clouds. The poem is directly preserved in Xuedou's collected verses, rather than known only through later accounts. Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「學人擬渡龍門，乞師一接。」師以拂子作釣勢，僧擬再語，師云：「領取鉤頭意，莫認定盤星。」問：「從上宗乘本是一個鼻孔，為什麼後代分宗列派？請師明示。」師云：「裂破舌頭。」進云：「如何是臨濟宗？」師云：「一棒打殺。」「如何是雲門宗？」師云：「一喝便死。」「如何是溈仰宗？」師云：「想你跳他圓相不出。」「如何是曹洞宗？」師云：「待你死了活來道。」「如何是法眼宗？」師舉起拂子云：「會麼？」進云：「五家宗派蒙師指，未知和尚是誰宗？」師與當頭一棒，云：「試為老僧分析看。」乃云：「入門便見賓主歷然，開眼便明萬彙齊現，若向賓主歷然處會，未免無名立名、無相見相，遂見天是天、地是地、山是山、水是水、僧是僧、俗是俗、男是男、女是女、佛是佛、祖是祖，種種差殊；若向萬彙齊現處見，則天不是天、地不是地、山不是山、水不是水、僧不是僧、俗不是俗、男不是男、女不是女、佛不是佛、祖不是祖、賓不是賓、主不是主，一道平等，浩然大均。且兩頭不涉，獨脫一句作麼生道？還委悉麼？雲有出山勢，水無投澗聲。」便下座。上堂。「今朝十月十六，天色陰晴反覆，不欲隨世變遷，悟取本來面目。已過關者，聞恁麼道，掉臂而去，二六時中折旋俯仰，無非本地風光；脫未諳悉，二六時中未免業識茫茫無本可據，且如何是本來面目？」喝一喝，云：「還見麼？地缺東南，天空西北。」復喝一喝，下座。上堂。

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 天是天，地是地，山是山，水是水

Senses.Explanation: Heaven is heaven and earth is earth is a plain declaration that things appear under their ordinary differentiated names. Miyun Yuanwu sets the sequence against an opposite “heaven is not heaven” sequence and then refuses confinement to either side. Baichi Xingyuan says heaven, earth, mountains, water, people, and things each occupy their place, while Yunmen Kuangzhen directly tells the assembly not to fantasize before giving the same list. The wording states ordinary differentiation; it is not itself a final doctrine.

Senses.Note: Juelang says the pair after rain; Zuliang uses it as the opening of his own verse; Yushan voices it in a current sermon; Xueyan puts it among visible and audible events when asking where Buddha and teaching are absent. An earlier anthology also transmits it as a verse by Miaozhan, but this selection counts four separate current deployments. The ordinary observation is the point of the encounter, not a weather forecast.

Occurrences.Kwic: 「南無消災延壽藥師佛。此猶是教意邊事，祖師門下又且不然。拈須彌於一毫頭上、擲大千於蟭螟眼裡，直得東海波騰、嵩獄作舞，雲自呈祥、香煙合彩。向者裏著得隻眼，鑑徹古今，纖毫無間，隨施一機，千機萬機透露；展演一句，千句萬句洞明。頭頭顯本有風光，物物彰未生面目。所以，我方母老孺人八十年中受用不盡底，皆秉此個恩力。」揮拂子，云：「大眾看看，無量壽如來與應供諸菩薩、方廣五百流，飽飫香齋在拂子頭上。一齊合掌，云：『人間慶大椿，菊花爛熳新，更有多意氣，貴子產祥麟。』」下座。佛誕日，化城吉祥庵主佛開光，化三禪德領眾善信恭請小參。師云：「今朝四月八，處處慶悉達，昔日老雲門，一棒要打殺，千古播英風，嘉聲惡辣辣。化城諸善人，信心猛自發，金軀煥然新，光明遍塵剎。作者蒙斯光，咸受佛慈拔，天上與人間，生生獲妙樂。雖然，且道昔日雲門打殺的是？今諸善人裝金的是？若向者裡定當得去，釋迦老子在你諸人面門出入，動地放光，二六時中不曾違背一絲毫許。其或未然，聽取山僧一偈：天晴日頭出，雨落地下濕，陰晴雖不同，兩不失其節。」下座。張維翰、維藩、維屏三孝嗣為薦先嚴華椿居士請對靈小參。師云：「初夏方臨，鶯啼綠樹，大唱圓音，誰人聽？」驀豎拂，云：「突出一句，明如杲日，迥脫根塵，輝天鑒地，裂破愛見情網，截斷生死根株，直透威音那畔纖毫不立，顯示今世門頭全機獨露。向者裡見徹根源，便知我華椿居士昔日親登翔鳳與山僧聚談道話亦未曾生，即今幻緣報謝、靈光不昧又何曾滅？既爾生滅一如、去來不異，且道畢竟在甚麼處安身立命？花雨繽紛際，蓮臺敷坐時。」擊拂子，下座。園花陳御卿居士請為二嚴慈點主。師舉筆云：「秪者一點，獲之象帝之先，迥越物情之表，靈然獨露，塵劫難磨。諸佛證之，出三界九有；歷代祖師悟之，流通正眼；天地得之，昫嫗萬物；人君得之，掌握乾坤；臣宰得之，輔齊家國；在我陳公居士得之，作冥途慧炬，起嗣胤芳聲。且道者一點畢竟落在甚麼處？」遂點云：「浩浩塵中能作主，人間天上獨為尊。」平湖德藏禪寺語錄卷二門人廣和記錄住平湖德藏禪寺語錄康熙三十三年九月二十一日進院。即日，當道眾紳衿、護法並本山諸耆德請師陞座。僧問：「德藏名剎，特峙東湖，懸花雨之舊亭，存松風之遺跡。和尚到來，如何是重整一句？」師云：「萬象盡含新。」進云：「高提祖印，棒喝交馳，不涉二途，又作

Occurrences.Kwic: 一統乾坤，有殃害平人之惡，被拂子一時擒下，縛作一束，號令在這裡了也。還見麼？若也未見，待與從頭點過。以拂子擊一下，三玄三要；又擊一下，五位君臣；又擊一下，一鏃破三關，分明箭後路；又擊一下，三界惟心，萬法惟識；又擊一下，絲來線去，明暗相投。既是贓證一一分明，如今却作麼生結絕？連擊兩下。乃云：佛法無人說，雖慧不能了。只如諸方老宿匡徒領眾三百、五百、一千，浩浩地擊動牛皮皷、擺動牛尾巴，又豈是無說？又如盡大地人著衣免寒、喫飯免饑，更要了箇什麼？又何待你板頭下一箇黃面漢子攙匙亂筯、搖唇鼓舌作什麼？雖然，你畢竟喚什麼作佛？又喚什麼作法？了與不了又作麼生？忽若有箇生鐵鑄就底漢捩轉面皮，喝散大眾，掀倒禪床，豈不慶快平生，話行天下？若是邯鄲學唐步，放過也恐未得在。有麼？有麼？現前諸尊上，既是袖裡藏鋒，冷觀敗闕，莫怪向淨潔地上撮些子沙土，撒在你後生晚進眼裏去也。山河大地，明暗色空，豈不是佛是法？風動塵起，鴉鳴鵲噪，豈不是佛是法？四時代謝，萬物榮枯，天晴日頭出，雨落地下濕，豈不是佛是法？以至真如般若，菩提涅槃，無明煩惱，妄想顛倒，行住坐臥，折旋俯仰，豈不是佛是法？這箇是諸方叢林中學得底家常茶飯，有什麼交涉？既無交涉，又莫是泥龕塑像，黃卷赤軸，是佛是法麼？又莫是即心非心，亦有亦無，半合半開，是佛是法麼？又莫是麻三斤，乾屎橛，庭前栢樹子，是佛是法麼？又莫是觀世音將錢買胡餅，放下手元來是饅頭，蝦䗫𨁝跳上天，蚯蚓驀過東海，是佛是法麼？又莫是盡一千七百則主賓互換生殺之機，與一大藏五時八教權實之旨，是佛是法麼？這箇又是諸方老凍膿嘔出底野狐涎唾，又有什麼交涉？既無交涉，又莫是即今口吧吧地與眼眨眨地，是佛是法麼？這箇喚作鼓無明袋，弄粥飯氣，沒交涉中更沒交涉。既無交涉，畢竟佛法二字却教甚麼人說？又教甚麼處了？喝一喝。若是師子，便合翻身，韓獹一任逐塊。所以道：赤肉團上，壁立萬仞，只此靈鋒，阿誰敢擬？亦能殺人，亦能活人，奴呼菩薩，婢視聲聞。釋迦老子只好提瓶挈水，達磨大師洗脚也未有分。據生死海，為大解脫遊戲之場；滅佛祖燈，如彼夢幻空花之影。無去無來，無得無失，無古無今，無他無自，空牢牢，活潑潑，淨倮倮，赤洒洒，沒可把。明明向你道沒可把，因什麼十箇五雙動是扶籬摸壁，無自由分？又如駝一箇漢子在肩上立地了，行一步子也放手

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 「南無消災延壽藥師佛。此猶是教意邊事，祖師門下又且不然。拈須彌於一毫頭上、擲大千於蟭螟眼裡，直得東海波騰、嵩獄作舞，雲自呈祥、香煙合彩。向者裏著得隻眼，鑑徹古今，纖毫無間，隨施一機，千機萬機透露；展演一句，千句萬句洞明。頭頭顯本有風光，物物彰未生面目。所以，我方母老孺人八十年中受用不盡底，皆秉此個恩力。」揮拂子，云：「大眾看看，無量壽如來與應供諸菩薩、方廣五百流，飽飫香齋在拂子頭上。一齊合掌，云：『人間慶大椿，菊花爛熳新，更有多意氣，貴子產祥麟。』」下座。佛誕日，化城吉祥庵主佛開光，化三禪德領眾善信恭請小參。師云：「今朝四月八，處處慶悉達，昔日老雲門，一棒要打殺，千古播英風，嘉聲惡辣辣。化城諸善人，信心猛自發，金軀煥然新，光明遍塵剎。作者蒙斯光，咸受佛慈拔，天上與人間，生生獲妙樂。雖然，且道昔日雲門打殺的是？今諸善人裝金的是？若向者裡定當得去，釋迦老子在你諸人面門出入，動地放光，二六時中不曾違背一絲毫許。其或未然，聽取山僧一偈：天晴日頭出，雨落地下濕，陰晴雖不同，兩不失其節。」下座。張維翰、維藩、維屏三孝嗣為薦先嚴華椿居士請對靈小參。師云：「初夏方臨，鶯啼綠樹，大唱圓音，誰人聽？」驀豎拂，云：「突出一句，明如杲日，迥脫根塵，輝天鑒地，裂破愛見情網，截斷生死根株，直透威音那畔纖毫不立，顯示今世門頭全機獨露。向者裡見徹根源，便知我華椿居士昔日親登翔鳳與山僧聚談道話亦未曾生，即今幻緣報謝、靈光不昧又何曾滅？既爾生滅一如、去來不異，且道畢竟在甚麼處安身立命？花雨繽紛際，蓮臺敷坐時。」擊拂子，下座。園花陳御卿居士請為二嚴慈點主。師舉筆云：「秪者一點，獲之象帝之先，迥越物情之表，靈然獨露，塵劫難磨。諸佛證之，出三界九有；歷代祖師悟之，流通正眼；天地得之，昫嫗萬物；人君得之，掌握乾坤；臣宰得之，輔齊家國；在我陳公居士得之，作冥途慧炬，起嗣胤芳聲。且道者一點畢竟落在甚麼處？」遂點云：「浩浩塵中能作主，人間天上獨為尊。」平湖德藏禪寺語錄卷二門人廣和記錄住平湖德藏禪寺語錄康熙三十三年九月二十一日進院。即日，當道眾紳衿、護法並本山諸耆德請師陞座。僧問：「德藏名剎，特峙東湖，懸花雨之舊亭，存松風之遺跡。和尚到來，如何是重整一句？」師云：「萬象盡含新。」進云：「高提祖印，棒喝交馳，不涉二途，又作

Senses.Explanation: Heaven covers all without preference; earth bears all without preference. The paired heaven and earth image names impartial care or reception. The source-backed uses include Tian'an Sheng in J26nB187, Yushan Shangsi in J40nB494, Fushi Tongxian in J26nB185, Yinyuan Longqi in J27nB193, and Binya Jian in J28nB204. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. Several uses occur in ritual praise; their shared metaphor does not turn into a specific policy claim.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山頂頭有一比丘，字曰覺圜，嚴修戒定，旌崇道德，佗日靈山會上又添一座，門弟子眾依佗方便，勤修十善，供養三尊。後來善法堂中又添數人，因為此事，特來賀喜。』世尊曰：『善哉！善哉！惟願四天之下、萬國之中，個個嚴修戒定，入聖超凡，旌崇道德，積功累行，勤修十善，果感人天，供養三尊，咸超苦趣。』說是語時，天雨寶花，繽紛亂墜，地搖六種，悉皆震動，驚得須菩提在巖壑中宴坐不下，倉忙速赴靈山，一手搊住文殊曰：『大士！大士！我且問汝，當時已在楞嚴會上道個見聞如幻翳，三界若空花，聞復翳根除，塵銷覺圜淨，如許法塵向甚麼處銷？這段玅覺向甚麼處圜？你若道得這兩轉語不謬，稱為七佛之師；若道不得，搥折獅子腰去。』大士被佗一問，逼得無言可申、無理可對，觸發金毛獅子奮迅出來，大吼一聲，各各逡巡而退。山僧從斯而覺，默默靜聽，下方罔明大士彈指一下，百億世尊光徹梵天，二乘聲聞無見頂相。未審眾中還有單為文殊大士出氣者麼？便與旗山相見；不然，還請木上座代渠出氣去也。」驀拈拄杖云：「意未涉簾纖，孤光徹梵天，儼然成一片，何處不圜圜？」喝一喝，卓杖下座。元正大念大德請上堂。僧問：「玉曆早頒即不問，春王行令事若何？」師云：「萬木叨光彩，千山總色新。」進云：「園裏百花猶未放，山間何物出頭來？」師云：「靈梅戰出雪，特露顯東君。」問：「如何是新年境？」師云：「黃葉未曾掃，時來樹又青。」進云：「如何是舊年人？」師云：「淺水觀魚躍，輕煙看鳥飛。」進云：「只逢擺尾拖泥過，未見搖頭解攫雲。」師云：「既有解攫，何不下手？」僧擬議，師便喝，僧亦喝，師打云：「這掠虛漢。」乃云：「艸木青秀，花雨芳菲，萬象發輝，千峰擁翠。雷驚深蟄，頻頻變動；風和幽鳥，數數轉聲。水涌波瀾，獰龍跳躍；林生瑞氣，埜鶴飛騰。物物造化，俱皆承斯恩力；個個圜光，無不觸處發現。所以道：天然上士，豈受提撕？中下之機，鉤頭取則。且不立言詞一句作麼生道？迷時實有三乘教，悟後了無一字關。」復舉：「真淨和尚問一座主曰：『火災起時，山河大地俱皆焚盡，世間虛空是否？』主對曰：『教有明文，安有不是之理？』淨曰：『如許多灰燼將置向何處？』主無對，淨曰：『汝所講者，紙上語耳。』」師云：「涵清之月，未免明中墮影；延木之蔓，不覺暗裏抽條。當時有個衲僧在數，待佗道：『如許多灰燼將置向何處？』不妨上前對面一吹，管取老大真淨當下結舌而退。還識落處麼？於此識得，玅中更有玅、奇中更有奇；若也未能，行腳不開如是眼，艸鞋終被石頭欺。」下座。上堂。舉：「南泉、魯祖、杉山、歸宗同喫茶次，魯祖拈起茶盞云：『世界未成時便有這個。』南泉云：『今人只識這個，未識世界。』宗云：『是。』泉云：『師兄莫同此見麼？』宗拈起盞云：『向世界未成時道得麼？』泉作掌勢，宗以面來接掌。」師云：「一個把函就蓋，一個把蓋就函，一人不得受用，一人被他埋卻，縱辨得出，不知這夥破落戶是何心行？頌曰：元宵美景月升天，爽氣清和夜不眠，見得時光人快樂，頻添燈火慶豐年。」下座。解制，上堂。僧問：「古人道：『有佛處即不住』，意旨如何？」師云：「住則三十棒。」進云：「『無佛處急走過』，又作麼生？」師云：「金鱗衝散浮萍綠，玉驥蹋翻掩路青。」進云：「衲僧行徑蒙師指，涉遍歸來事若何？」師云：「鳥歇山自靜，花罷樹梢閒。」僧禮拜，師拈拄杖，云：「結從此處結，疑團未破豈休歇？」卓一下，云：「解從此處解，靈光晃耀知端楷。如是，則塵塵皆聖制，剎剎圜覺海；不然，逐境迷一生，順世流千載。若是超群人，自然覺方採，鳳凰必不入雞栖，獅子終無戀兔嬭，鐵鑄饅頭仔細吞，充饑畫餅休勞買。既然如此，如何保任？蔕固不愁結果時，花開切忌風來擺。」下座。廣福山勝覺寺密印禪師語錄卷第三廣福山勝覺
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J35/J35nB343.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyin of Shengjue Monastery, Guangfu Mountain. Miyin Zhenchuan describes spring vegetation, changing birdsong, leaping dragons and flying cranes as receiving the same generative force, with each person's clear light appearing wherever it meets things. He then introduces the inherited formula: why would one naturally of the highest capacity need prompting, while those of middle or lower capacity take their standard from the hook? Asking for a sentence that does not establish words, he answers that delusion has its three paths of instruction but awakening has no barrier made of a single word. He goes on to raise Zhenjing's challenge to a lecturer about where the ashes of a world-consuming fire would be put, and proposes that a monk could have approached and blown in the teacher's face. That is Miyin's suggested response, not an action the record says a monk actually performed. The exact headword remains an unnamed earlier formula voice; Miyin's current use tests received explanations through an imagined direct encounter rather than stopping all teaching.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. After questions about the Buddha's first steps and awakening on seeing the morning star, Yushan Shangsi says that the practitioner's gate has no planned arrangements: the occasion values naturalness and activity is already present. Going freely on foot, he says, opens release at every point, and freely moving the hand reveals the actual appearance everywhere. Why insist that seeing a star at night or hearing horns in the morning must first certify awakening? He then revoices the highest-capacity question in his own address and contrasts it with taking a standard from the hook. He urges hearers to cast off the bindings of Buddhas and ancestors and overturn the habitual nests of ordinary and holy, then asks for a sentence of independent freedom. Waving his whisk, he replies that a man has his own sky-reaching resolve and does not follow the Buddha's footsteps. The headword is Yushan's present revoicing here, set amid his own questions and gesture, not a report that someone has attained a permanently certified rank.

Senses.Explanation: A person naturally of the highest capacity—why would they need prompting? Miyin Zhenchuan describes spring vegetation, changing birdsong, leaping dragons and flying cranes as receiving the same generative force, with each person's clear light appearing wherever it meets things. He then introduces the inherited formula: why would one naturally of the highest capacity need prompting, while those of middle or lower capacity take their standard from the hook? Asking for a sentence that does not establish words, he answers that delusion has its three paths of instruction but awakening has no barrier made of a single word. He goes on to raise Zhenjing's challenge to a lecturer about where the ashes of a world-consuming fire would be put, and proposes that a monk could have approached and blown in the teacher's face. That is Miyin's suggested response, not an action the record says a monk actually performed. The exact headword remains an unnamed earlier formula voice; Miyin's current use tests received explanations through an imagined direct encounter rather than stopping all teaching. After questions about the Buddha's first steps and awakening on seeing the morning star, Yushan Shangsi says that the practitioner's gate has no planned arrangements: the occasion values naturalness and activity is already present. Going freely on foot, he says, opens release at every point, and freely moving the hand reveals the actual appearance everywhere. Why insist that seeing a star at night or hearing horns in the morning must first certify awakening? He then revoices the highest-capacity question in his own address and contrasts it with taking a standard from the hook. He urges hearers to cast off the bindings of Buddhas and ancestors and overturn the habitual nests of ordinary and holy, then asks for a sentence of independent freedom. Waving his whisk, he replies that a man has his own sky-reaching resolve and does not follow the Buddha's footsteps. The headword is Yushan's present revoicing here, set amid his own questions and gesture, not a report that someone has attained a permanently certified rank. The lamp names the speaker Ruru Ji. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu supplies answers and further challenges to eleven older questions attributed to Zhimen Zuo. One asks for a statement right now, setting aside thirty years before and after and warning that failure at one point loses both. Tianyin answers that heaven and earth endure and sun and moon shine together, then caps it with 'universal' and asks how the assembly would answer. The exact pair is Tianyin's present answer to the raised question, not Zhimen's original utterance. Its broad temporal and luminous imagery is immediately returned to a fresh demand for speech, rather than offered as a final cosmological explanation of the present.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi Mingyu raises a monk asking Shoushan Xingnian what Buddha is. Shoushan answers with a bride riding a donkey led by her mother-in-law. Asked what category of sentence this belongs to, he says neither the three mysteries nor four sentences can encompass it. When the monk asks its meaning, Shoushan gives the enduring heaven and earth and jointly shining sun and moon. Sanyi follows with a terse cap involving a lacquer chicken's head and a general removing lice from a wall. The exact pair belongs to Shoushan's quoted reply, not Sanyi; the opaque later cap should not be smoothed into an explicit endorsement or a neatly decoded teaching category.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB287.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zixianjue. At Zixian Jue's New Year address, an unnamed monk requests a blessing for the ruler amid spring winds and golden willow shoots. Zixian replies with gongs mingling with drums; the monk then offers enduring heaven and earth and sun and moon shining together. Zixian asks where his heels stand. A shout earns 'good shout,' but after the bow the teacher calls him an illicit salt dealer. The headword is the monk's answer, not Zixian's own blessing. The sequence mixes acceptance and renewed challenge, so neither the auspicious wording nor the praise of the shout alone certifies the speaker's realization. The monk is not individually named in this episode.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB424.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xiangyan. At Puming Xiangyan's New Year address, a monk asks what the ancestral household looks like amid festive drums and firecrackers. Puming first gives a plum branch in the slanting sun. Asked for a sentence blessing the ruler, he answers with enduring heaven and earth and jointly shining sun and moon. Further questions about public prosperity receive household incense and plum flowers, but a request for the fundamental sentence receives thirty blows. Puming then raises his staff and asks where the new spring arises. Here the headword is a current auspicious answer within a differentiated exchange; the later challenge prevents ceremonial language from exhausting the instruction. The source names Puming Xiangyan without establishing a canonical lineage identity.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB448.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lingji. In Lingji Xingguan's morning instruction, an unnamed monk says recognition before words and acceptance under a shout still fail, and asks what would suffice. Lingji says he knows the monk has no resting place. The monk asserts immediate presentation without opposition and a single point spanning ancient and present; asked what spans them, he answers with enduring heaven and earth and jointly shining sun and moon. Lingji calls this still a matter of explaining principles. The headword belongs to the monk's offered answer and receives an explicit reservation. This witness therefore shows the formula failing as a present response, not the teacher endorsing the cosmological description as sufficient.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu supplies answers and further challenges to eleven older questions attributed to Zhimen Zuo. One asks for a statement right now, setting aside thirty years before and after and warning that failure at one point loses both. Tianyin answers that heaven and earth endure and sun and moon shine together, then caps it with 'universal' and asks how the assembly would answer. The exact pair is Tianyin's present answer to the raised question, not Zhimen's original utterance. Senses.PreferredTarget: Heaven is high to the southeast; earth tilts to the northwest
SearchAliases: heaven is high to the southeast; earth tilts to the northwest
Senses.Note: “Heaven is high to the southeast; earth tilts to the northwest” gives an uneven landscape where a listener expects a tidy answer. Baochi says it when asked how to speak of before, after, and both together in relation to the Buddha. Yanxi offers it as his own answer to where emptiness returns after all colors return to emptiness. Dachuan uses the line when asking what path of emergence a newly appointed master has. Wuzhun gives it after contrasting two earlier masters’ ways of wielding staff and shout. The line points the audience into each live question through a deliberately lopsided picture.

Occurrences.Kwic: ，丁當。良久，云：會麼？願將如是曲，長奉聖明君。謝新舊知事，上堂。世諦門中，有新有舊，有出有入，有進有退；佛法向上，無高無下，無彼無此，無黨無偏。雖然如是，阿那箇些子是佛法？阿那箇些子是世諦？試為乳峯拈出一絲頭看。良久，云：放憨作麼？上堂。德山老漢平生據一條白棒，佛來也打，祖來也打，却道不曾打著一箇獨脫底興。他道：東廊也下喝，西廊也下喝。直饒你喝得興化上三十三天，撲下來一點氣也無。待興化緩緩地甦息起來，向你道未在。諸人還知二大老立處麼？天高東南，地傾西北。冬節，上堂：一冬二冬，叉手當𮌎。珠鑽九曲，直在其中。上堂。上元正月半，燈火連霄漢，千人與萬人，聚頭相共看。看即不無，第一各自照顧眼睛，乳峯不著，便末上打失了也。既是打失，將什麼辨緇素？良久，云：文殊頭白，普賢頭黑。上堂，舉：僧問馬大師：如何是祖師西來意？馬師云：近前來，向你道。僧近前，馬師與一掌，僧云：因甚打某甲？馬師云：六耳不同謀。後來黃龍南禪師道：古人尚道六耳不同謀，如今諸方浩浩商量禍事。師召大眾云：盡信書，不如無書。上堂：十方國

Senses.Explanation: A tilted heaven and earth answer questions that seek a neat location or division. Baochi voices the line to a student asking about before and after the Buddha. Yanxi gives it as his answer to a question about where emptiness goes. Dachuan and Wuzhun use the same skewed image in two separate sermons about finding a way through an encounter.

Entries.SourceTerm: 天高羣象正，海闊百川朝

Senses.PreferredTarget: With the sky high, the myriad forms stand in order; with the sea wide, a hundred rivers come to it
AlternateTargets: The high sky sets all forms in place, and the open sea receives every river
SearchAliases: high sky myriad forms wide sea hundred rivers Chan
all rivers flow to broad sea Zen
Senses.Note: High sky gives the many forms their setting; a broad sea receives the rivers. Wumen uses the pair after rejecting a narrower old answer. Songyuan, Wuzhun, and Shitian also give it as their own close or answer. The image is expansive: the sky and sea admit many things without making them identical.

Occurrences.Kwic: ，雨似盆傾。師云：乾峰坐在這裏，寸步不移。偃禪師脚不點地，全無定力。今日佛法委付在臣僧之手，把住則真金失色，放行則瓦礫生光。且道不把住、不放行一句又作麼生？一雨普霑沙界潤，萬姓謳歌喜氣回。久坐聖躬，伏惟珍重。師自十一日申時辭禁中歸寺，入後山靈洞默禱。十四日早，承直殿陳叔達傳旨來問：幾時雨？通等候回奏。師即答曰：寂然不動，感而遂通。回奏畢，當時有雨。十六日，伏承樞密吳相公惠頌曰：黑山心歷歷，金殿口巴巴。不因漁父引，怎得見波查？師即以偈答曰：出洞昂頭角，回山露尾巴。恩承饒舌力，累我受波查。上堂，舉溈山與仰山摘茶次，溈云：終日祇聞子聲，不見子形。仰山撼茶樹，溈山云：子只得其用，不得其體。仰山云：某甲祇如是，和尚作麼生？溈山據坐，仰山云：和尚祇得其體，不得其用。溈山云：放子三十棒。師頌云：針芥相投，體用俱全。衲僧門下，十萬八千。聖節，上堂。獅子叢林，獅子圍繞；旃檀叢林，旃檀圍繞。古人恁麼說話，見處偏枯。靈洞又且不然，畢竟如何？只向他道：天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。基宗二長老煎點，上堂。掀飜大地基方隱，起家還是破家兒，殺佛殺祖滅吾宗，箇是瞎驢施玅用。壁蟧食母，慈鵶返哺，一放一收，同歸異路。老僧隨處設箇鑽龜打瓦底鋪子，三十年後管取有人卜度。滿散聖節，上堂，舉：大宗皇帝幸開寶寺塔院，見僧問曰：卿是何人？僧曰：塔主。帝曰：寡人之塔，卿何作主？僧無語。後雪竇代云：闔國咸知。山僧敬成一頌，舉似諸人：名高不用鐫頑石，路上行人口是󳬴。大宋正傳天子令，直教諸國豎降旗。普賢生日，上堂：普賢行願等三千，正是清明首夏天。要見大人真境界，月明常照御樓前。浴佛，上堂。悉達太子初生下時，周行七步，目顧四方，一手指天、一手指地，天上天下惟吾獨尊。山僧聞知，甚是不甘。後聞雲門大師道：我當時若見，一棒打殺與狗子喫，貴圖天下太平。山僧甚是快意。又得波旬逼令涅槃，頗合公論。可憐四聖六凡皆被瞿曇誑惑，獨有山僧不隨他轉。且道山僧有甚長處？龍蛇易辨，衲子難瞞。開爐上堂：爛柴頭，火一團，急著眼，莫瞞盰。卓拄杖，星在秤兮不在盤。無門開和尚語錄卷上無門開和尚語錄卷下告香普說告香普說靈山密付黃葉止啼，少室親傳望梅止渴，乃至德山棒、臨濟喝、雪峰輥毬、道吾舞笏、祕魔擎叉、禾山打鼓、清原垂足、天龍豎指，盡是弄猢猻底閑家具，到者裏總用不著。雖

Occurrences.Kwic: 自九重降來；一段光明，如十日並照。千靈景仰，百谷風生，驗在目前，大家薦取。拈疏云：見成公案，未舉先知，不涉毫端，顯正法眼。儻或尚留觀聽，請為敷宣。上堂，僧問：道價遠聞天上去，宸恩今自日邊來。四眾仰瞻，願聞祝聖。師云：南嶽萬年松。進云：一言已祝南山壽，八表無私賀太平。師云：天闊地闊。進云：如何是第一句？師云：破燈盞。進云：如何是第二句？師云：裂破虗空。進云：如何是第三句？師云：斬釘截鐵。進云：擘破華山雷未迅，照開滄海月非光。師云：也尋常。進云：僧問百丈：如何是奇特事？丈云：獨坐大雄峰。此意如何？師云：話墮也。進云：未審向甚處見百丈？師豎起拂子云：還見麼？進云：非惟佛日重輝，亦乃叢林有賴。師云：只是蹉過百丈𠰚。僧禮拜。師乃云：祖師心印，狀似鐵牛之機，去即印住，住即印破。若也不去不住，全機大用，觸處流輝，溢目清光，貫通今古，發揮正法眼藏，傳持佛祖心宗，玅用縱橫，頭頭合轍，直得堯天舜日共樂昇平，鼓腹謳歌，歸家穩坐。且道當陽一句作麼生道？天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。復舉三聖道：我逢人則出，出則不為人。興化道：我逢人則不出，出則便為人。師拈云：二老漢滅却臨濟正法眼，却向長安路上把手共行，直至如今󳯝相鈍置。且如何是共行一句？掣開金殿鏁，撞碎玉樓鐘。松源和尚語錄卷上松源和尚語錄卷下臨安府景德靈隱禪寺語錄臨安府景德靈隱禪寺語錄參學道巖等錄慶元三年六月五日入院，指三門云：靈山一路，達者猶迷，不立堦梯，憑誰措足？到頭相見無餘事，月下披雲嘯一聲。指法座云：要行便行，要坐便坐，水長船高，泥多佛大。陞座，拈香云：此一瓣香，恭為祝延今上皇帝聖壽無疆，萬歲萬歲萬萬歲。次拈香云：此一瓣香，奉為丞相國公．闔朝文武百官資陪祿筭。次拈香云：此香爇向爐中，供養前住當山後住天童密庵先師大和尚，用酬法乳。遂就座。僧問：鼓響鐘鳴談實相，燈籠露柱放毫光。不須更覓長安路，已是全身入帝鄉。學人上來，請師答話。師竪起拂子，云：還見麼？進云：只這住山非有意，向來成佛亦無心。師云：相隨來也。進云：昔日圓悟禪師示眾道：有一人不離家舍，常在半途；有一人常在半途，不離家舍。意旨如何？師云：金剛手中八楞棒。進云：今日和尚在家，舍在半途。師云：鶖子神通不奈何。進云：恁麼則今朝喜得主人歸。師云：一時坐斷。進云：昔日王常侍訪臨濟，問：好一堂僧，為

Occurrences.Kwic: 活計。絕緣而照，離念而知，言發非聲，色前不物。塵塵爾，剎剎爾，圓融無際；巍巍乎，蕩蕩乎，綿亘有餘。舒卷自由，縱橫得妙。且坐斷千差一句作麼生道？四海浪平龍睡穩，九天雲淨鳳來儀。復舉：僧問太平恩禪師：日未出時如何？恩云：眾人皆仰望。又問：日出後如何？恩云：萬里照無私。師云：太平恁麼答話，可謂應時應節。徑山今日更資一路，或有問：日未出時如何？只向佗道：在。日出後如何？却向佗道：普。若更問：徑山是臨濟兒孫，因甚闡雲門宗旨？向道：千車自古無歧轍，四海如今共一家。謝首座、維那，上堂。黃蘗赴堂，無端向南泉位；中座興化行令，從而逐出克賓。父不父、子不子、弟不弟、兄不兄，千載令人恨不平。如今莫有報不平底麼？良久，云：吽！吽！朝廷撥賜萬年正續院產業。上堂：田地穩密，不妨蕩蕩乾坤。寶印發輝，又見重重光彩。得之諦當，用處玲瓏。普濟貧乏而有餘，饜飽飢虗而無盡。而使狂者息，昧者明，來者安，去者適。無無不是，箇箇歸源。法法全彰，頭頭有據。正恁麼時，恩歸何所？天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。復云：曉來瑞氣󳬂怱怱，流出恩波自九重。地厚天高何以報，飽看南嶽祝融峯。孟少保為石田和尚齋僧，請上堂。靈山密付，少室單傳，的的相承，綿綿不墜，不論緇黃青紫，大都達者為親。是故，韓文公肯首於大顛；裴相國印心於黃蘗；李駙馬參石門，著手心頭便判；龐居士見馬祖，一口吸盡西江。此皆從上真宗，古今一貫。我石田師兄末後句子固不容易今付，而無庵居士亦不容易承當，膠漆相投，繩繩有在。然這一片田地，四至界畔契券分明，幸有當人一時承紹了也。惟中間樹子，莫怪徑山却有分在。何故？無蔕花頭須結子，不萌枝上要抽條。復云：前日無庵以石田拳頭塞石田鼻孔，後來靈隱癡絕，凡以無庵拳頭塞無庵鼻孔，逗到徑山。這裏無拳頭可用，未免却借鼻孔特為出氣去也。石田不下尋常種，一味深耕種蒺藜，沒興有人親踏著，痛連心髓血淋漓。此恨難雪，此悔難追，慢罵呪詛，活陷泥犁。這般冤結何時解？直待虗空落地時。上堂：達磨西來，不立文字，直指人心，見性成佛。甞聞大亂之本生乎堯舜之間，其末存乎千載之後，千載之後其必有人與人相食者也。誠哉是言！解制，上堂，舉：岳林振禪師示眾云：布袋口開，還有買賣底麼？時有僧云：有。振云：不作貴，不作賤，作麼生買？僧無語。振云：老僧失利。師云：岳林設箇問頭，也似從容閑

Occurrences.Kwic: 寺語錄臨安府淨慈報恩光孝禪寺語錄嗣法門人了覺師坦等編入三門，示眾云：慧日峯高，門庭壁立，放一線開，從這裏入。據方丈云：一徑直，二周遮，擒虎兕，辨龍蛇，白玉無瑕却有瑕。拈勑黃云：九重降旨，闔國咸知，一句當頭，諸人未委。只如新長老還委麼？良久，云：寧可截舌，不犯國諱。登座示眾云：向上一路，千聖不然，目前無異草，脚下有青天。遂驟步登座，拈香云：恭為祝延今上皇帝聖壽萬歲萬歲萬萬歲，恭願百千諸佛保聖壽於無疆，億萬斯年等金剛而不壞。此一瓣香，恭為皇太后祝延聖壽。伏願大安大榮，永對無窮之問；時萬時億，獨觀有道之長。此一瓣香，奉為少傅、樞使、大丞相、國公、大參相公、同知樞密相公、簽書樞密相公、判府、安撫、侍郎、都運、寶文、都承、合朝文武宷僚，資陪祿筭。伏願乃武乃文，盡忠盡孝，永作天朝柱石，長為聖主股肱。此一瓣香，奉為前住安吉州鳳山資福破菴大和尚，不圖報德酬恩，索性一番鈍置。遂欽衣就座。時有僧出問云：南屏山下，慧日峯前，選佛場開，請師祝聖。答云：天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。僧云：祝聖已蒙師指示，只如選佛場中，還有心空及第底麼？答云：人人常光現前，箇箇壁立萬仞。僧云：可中忽有个不入這保社和尚，還肯他也無？答云：三十拄杖，且行別時。僧云：何不當面分付？答云：不識痛痒漢。僧便禮拜。師乃云：見聞覺知是法，法離見聞覺知。未入南屏門，湖天蕩漾，魚鳥忘機；既入南屏門，樓閣崢嶸，金碧奪目。坐底見立底，立底見坐底，妙圓通悟，正在茲時，堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化。其或未然，新長老重重失利。復舉：太宗皇帝因僧朝見，乃問：卿近離甚處？僧云：廬山臥雲菴。太宗云：臥雲深處不朝天，因甚到此？僧無語。雪竇代云：難逃至化。師拈云：太宗大人具大見，這僧大智得大用，雪竇雖則不負來機，未免鰕跳不出。若是新長老，當時只對云：今日小出大遇。且道還契得聖意也無？良久，云：慣從五鳳樓前過，手握金鞭賀太平。謝執事，上堂。眾流成海，眾毛成毬，一棚俊鶻，儒雅風流。石田無一事，坐地看楊州。上堂：石田乍到，人事紛紛。拈得鼻孔，失却眼睛。佛法二字，不怕爛却。且聽諸方行棒喝。浙翁遺書至，上堂：千五百人善知識，不念吾宗正岑寂。五峯趯倒浪翻空，大地山河俱失色。金風體露，葉落歸根，只堪惆悵不堪陳。上堂：不結毗盧印，那弘古佛心。明月照幽谷，寒濤助夜砧。師云：法

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ，雨似盆傾。師云：乾峰坐在這裏，寸步不移。偃禪師脚不點地，全無定力。今日佛法委付在臣僧之手，把住則真金失色，放行則瓦礫生光。且道不把住、不放行一句又作麼生？一雨普霑沙界潤，萬姓謳歌喜氣回。久坐聖躬，伏惟珍重。師自十一日申時辭禁中歸寺，入後山靈洞默禱。十四日早，承直殿陳叔達傳旨來問：幾時雨？通等候回奏。師即答曰：寂然不動，感而遂通。回奏畢，當時有雨。十六日，伏承樞密吳相公惠頌曰：黑山心歷歷，金殿口巴巴。不因漁父引，怎得見波查？師即以偈答曰：出洞昂頭角，回山露尾巴。恩承饒舌力，累我受波查。上堂，舉溈山與仰山摘茶次，溈云：終日祇聞子聲，不見子形。仰山撼茶樹，溈山云：子只得其用，不得其體。仰山云：某甲祇如是，和尚作麼生？溈山據坐，仰山云：和尚祇得其體，不得其用。溈山云：放子三十棒。師頌云：針芥相投，體用俱全。衲僧門下，十萬八千。聖節，上堂。獅子叢林，獅子圍繞；旃檀叢林，旃檀圍繞。古人恁麼說話，見處偏枯。靈洞又且不然，畢竟如何？只向他道：天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。基宗二長老煎點，上堂。掀飜大地基方隱，起家還是破家兒，殺佛殺祖滅吾宗，箇是瞎驢施玅用。壁蟧食母，慈鵶返哺，一放一收，同歸異路。老僧隨處設箇鑽龜打瓦底鋪子，三十年後管取有人卜度。滿散聖節，上堂，舉：大宗皇帝幸開寶寺塔院，見僧問曰：卿是何人？僧曰：塔主。帝曰：寡人之塔，卿何作主？僧無語。後雪竇代云：闔國咸知。山僧敬成一頌，舉似諸人：名高不用鐫頑石，路上行人口是󳬴。大宋正傳天子令，直教諸國豎降旗。普賢生日，上堂：普賢行願等三千，正是清明首夏天。要見大人真境界，月明常照御樓前。浴佛，上堂。悉達太子初生下時，周行七步，目顧四方，一手指天、一手指地，天上天下惟吾獨尊。山僧聞知，甚是不甘。後聞雲門大師道：我當時若見，一棒打殺與狗子喫，貴圖天下太平。山僧甚是快意。又得波旬逼令涅槃，頗合公論。可憐四聖六凡皆被瞿曇誑惑，獨有山僧不隨他轉。且道山僧有甚長處？龍蛇易辨，衲子難瞞。開爐上堂：爛柴頭，火一團，急著眼，莫瞞盰。卓拄杖，星在秤兮不在盤。無門開和尚語錄卷上無門開和尚語錄卷下告香普說告香普說靈山密付黃葉止啼，少室親傳望梅止渴，乃至德山棒、臨濟喝、雪峰輥毬、道吾舞笏、祕魔擎叉、禾山打鼓、清原垂足、天龍豎指，盡是弄猢猻底閑家具，到者裏總用不著。雖

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 自九重降來；一段光明，如十日並照。千靈景仰，百谷風生，驗在目前，大家薦取。拈疏云：見成公案，未舉先知，不涉毫端，顯正法眼。儻或尚留觀聽，請為敷宣。上堂，僧問：道價遠聞天上去，宸恩今自日邊來。四眾仰瞻，願聞祝聖。師云：南嶽萬年松。進云：一言已祝南山壽，八表無私賀太平。師云：天闊地闊。進云：如何是第一句？師云：破燈盞。進云：如何是第二句？師云：裂破虗空。進云：如何是第三句？師云：斬釘截鐵。進云：擘破華山雷未迅，照開滄海月非光。師云：也尋常。進云：僧問百丈：如何是奇特事？丈云：獨坐大雄峰。此意如何？師云：話墮也。進云：未審向甚處見百丈？師豎起拂子云：還見麼？進云：非惟佛日重輝，亦乃叢林有賴。師云：只是蹉過百丈𠰚。僧禮拜。師乃云：祖師心印，狀似鐵牛之機，去即印住，住即印破。若也不去不住，全機大用，觸處流輝，溢目清光，貫通今古，發揮正法眼藏，傳持佛祖心宗，玅用縱橫，頭頭合轍，直得堯天舜日共樂昇平，鼓腹謳歌，歸家穩坐。且道當陽一句作麼生道？天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。復舉三聖道：我逢人則出，出則不為人。興化道：我逢人則不出，出則便為人。師拈云：二老漢滅却臨濟正法眼，却向長安路上把手共行，直至如今󳯝相鈍置。且如何是共行一句？掣開金殿鏁，撞碎玉樓鐘。松源和尚語錄卷上松源和尚語錄卷下臨安府景德靈隱禪寺語錄臨安府景德靈隱禪寺語錄參學道巖等錄慶元三年六月五日入院，指三門云：靈山一路，達者猶迷，不立堦梯，憑誰措足？到頭相見無餘事，月下披雲嘯一聲。指法座云：要行便行，要坐便坐，水長船高，泥多佛大。陞座，拈香云：此一瓣香，恭為祝延今上皇帝聖壽無疆，萬歲萬歲萬萬歲。次拈香云：此一瓣香，奉為丞相國公．闔朝文武百官資陪祿筭。次拈香云：此香爇向爐中，供養前住當山後住天童密庵先師大和尚，用酬法乳。遂就座。僧問：鼓響鐘鳴談實相，燈籠露柱放毫光。不須更覓長安路，已是全身入帝鄉。學人上來，請師答話。師竪起拂子，云：還見麼？進云：只這住山非有意，向來成佛亦無心。師云：相隨來也。進云：昔日圓悟禪師示眾道：有一人不離家舍，常在半途；有一人常在半途，不離家舍。意旨如何？師云：金剛手中八楞棒。進云：今日和尚在家，舍在半途。師云：鶖子神通不奈何。進云：恁麼則今朝喜得主人歸。師云：一時坐斷。進云：昔日王常侍訪臨濟，問：好一堂僧，為

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 活計。絕緣而照，離念而知，言發非聲，色前不物。塵塵爾，剎剎爾，圓融無際；巍巍乎，蕩蕩乎，綿亘有餘。舒卷自由，縱橫得妙。且坐斷千差一句作麼生道？四海浪平龍睡穩，九天雲淨鳳來儀。復舉：僧問太平恩禪師：日未出時如何？恩云：眾人皆仰望。又問：日出後如何？恩云：萬里照無私。師云：太平恁麼答話，可謂應時應節。徑山今日更資一路，或有問：日未出時如何？只向佗道：在。日出後如何？却向佗道：普。若更問：徑山是臨濟兒孫，因甚闡雲門宗旨？向道：千車自古無歧轍，四海如今共一家。謝首座、維那，上堂。黃蘗赴堂，無端向南泉位；中座興化行令，從而逐出克賓。父不父、子不子、弟不弟、兄不兄，千載令人恨不平。如今莫有報不平底麼？良久，云：吽！吽！朝廷撥賜萬年正續院產業。上堂：田地穩密，不妨蕩蕩乾坤。寶印發輝，又見重重光彩。得之諦當，用處玲瓏。普濟貧乏而有餘，饜飽飢虗而無盡。而使狂者息，昧者明，來者安，去者適。無無不是，箇箇歸源。法法全彰，頭頭有據。正恁麼時，恩歸何所？天高羣象正，海闊百川朝。復云：曉來瑞氣󳬂怱怱，流出恩波自九重。地厚天高何以報，飽看南嶽祝融峯。孟少保為石田和尚齋僧，請上堂。靈山密付，少室單傳，的的相承，綿綿不墜，不論緇黃青紫，大都達者為親。是故，韓文公肯首於大顛；裴相國印心於黃蘗；李駙馬參石門，著手心頭便判；龐居士見馬祖，一口吸盡西江。此皆從上真宗，古今一貫。我石田師兄末後句子固不容易今付，而無庵居士亦不容易承當，膠漆相投，繩繩有在。然這一片田地，四至界畔契券分明，幸有當人一時承紹了也。惟中間樹子，莫怪徑山却有分在。何故？無蔕花頭須結子，不萌枝上要抽條。復云：前日無庵以石田拳頭塞石田鼻孔，後來靈隱癡絕，凡以無庵拳頭塞無庵鼻孔，逗到徑山。這裏無拳頭可用，未免却借鼻孔特為出氣去也。石田不下尋常種，一味深耕種蒺藜，沒興有人親踏著，痛連心髓血淋漓。此恨難雪，此悔難追，慢罵呪詛，活陷泥犁。這般冤結何時解？直待虗空落地時。上堂：達磨西來，不立文字，直指人心，見性成佛。甞聞大亂之本生乎堯舜之間，其末存乎千載之後，千載之後其必有人與人相食者也。誠哉是言！解制，上堂，舉：岳林振禪師示眾云：布袋口開，還有買賣底麼？時有僧云：有。振云：不作貴，不作賤，作麼生買？僧無語。振云：老僧失利。師云：岳林設箇問頭，也似從容閑

Senses.Explanation: The sky holds the many forms while the wide sea receives the rivers. Wumen and Songyuan use the pair to answer present questions about scope. Wuzhun and Shitian place it at the close of current questions about gathering and gratitude.

Entries.SourceTerm: 天高群象正，海闊百川朝

Senses.PreferredTarget: The sky is high and the myriad forms stand in order; the sea is wide and a hundred rivers pay court
AlternateTargets: High sky sets all forms in order; broad sea receives the homage of a hundred rivers
SearchAliases: high sky forms broad sea hundred rivers
Senses.Note: The paired sky and sea image sets the myriad forms in order under a high heaven and has the rivers turn toward a wide sea. Masters use it as a closing line or answer in teaching and ceremonial addresses.

Senses.Explanation: "The sky is high and the myriad forms stand in order; the sea is wide and a hundred rivers pay court" joins an ordered sky with a converging sea. Named masters use this complete couplet to answer a question or close an address. Wanru closes a hall address with it; Fushi gives it after hanging the board in another address. Linye answers a request for a celebratory line, and Tianan answers a question about a lion emerging. Sanyi closes a teaching turn with the image; Guxue gives it as a direct answer. Shipu answers a request for one sentence, while Tianshu uses the couplet in an opening blessing.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB392.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao. Hansong invokes the one-finger emblem at the end of his own funeral fire address as an immediate exhortation.

Senses.Explanation: Tianlong one finger: the inherited emblem of Juzhi realization and his later single-finger teaching. Juzhi original claim survives in the lamp; Weian and Poshan use it in separate teachings. Sanyi sets the emblem against his own present instruction; Chaozong composes a verse on it; Hansong makes it a closing exhortation in a funeral address. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: The eight classes of celestial beings and dragons are the inherited nonhuman audience and protector groups attending Buddhist assemblies. Yongming Yanshou gives the canonical collective; the bell inscription and Yinyuan-line assembly source summon it as an immediate audience, and Juelang Daosheng names it in an encounter setting. The four witnesses support a grouped audience, not eight interchangeable synonyms or one individual deity.
